process_map.summary: Customers send purchase orders via Person 1, triggering internal stock checks with Person 3 and invoice generation by Person 2. After Person 1 approves the invoice and transporter logistics are arranged, the goods are dispatched, LRs are collected, and Tally is updated while payment follow-ups are tracked continuously.

steps.name: Create and Send Invoice for Approval

pain_points.description: Invoice approvals take significant time, often requiring multiple gentle reminders from office staff.
Dispatches are delayed waiting for transporter availability or scheduled pickup times.
Pricing errors in invoices require corrections and issuing revised invoices.
Continuous follow-ups are required to track pending customer payments.
Delays in checking stock levels from the godown stall order processing.

analysis.top_insight: The biggest bottleneck is the multi-hour waiting gap caused by manual stock checks and invoice approvals. Integrating Tally live stock into your operational sheets and auto-approving standard orders will drastically cut down order-to-dispatch time.

steps.name: Receive Customer Purchase Order
steps.reason: Customer POs arrive as unstructured WhatsApp PDFs that need reading and manual forwarding.
steps.idea: Use an affordable AI parser to extract PO text and automatically drop it into a shared Google Sheet.

steps.name: Check Inventory Stock
steps.reason: Staff waste hours waiting and manually checking physical stock against digital orders.
steps.idea: Connect your Tally inventory directly to a shared Google Sheet so staff see live stock instantly without calling.

steps.name: Determine Partial or Full Dispatch
steps.reason: Deciding whether to hold out for full stock or ship partial quantities requires business owner judgement.
steps.idea: Keep the owner decision, but notify them instantly via WhatsApp summary when stock is short.

steps.name: Create and Send Invoice for Approval
steps.reason: Manual data entry between confirmed sheets and Tally creates pricing errors and rework.
steps.idea: Use a simple desktop automation or Tally connector to generate draft invoices automatically from approved quantities.

steps.name: Approve Invoice
steps.reason: Invoice approvals sit waiting for the owner, stalling the dispatch pipeline unnecessarily.
steps.idea: Implement an auto-approval rule in your workflow for trusted repeat customers below a set credit limit.

steps.name: Arrange Transporter and Prepare Dispatch
steps.reason: Arranging transporters involves variable local negotiations and physical logistics that cannot be fully rule-based.
steps.idea: Maintain standard transporter contact lists in a shared sheet for quick phone booking by staff.

steps.name: Physical Dispatch and LR Generation
steps.reason: Physical loading and LR collection at the godown are manual warehouse operations.
steps.idea: Have the warehouse staff snap a photo of the LR and drop it into a dedicated WhatsApp group immediately.

steps.name: Update Tally and Notify Customer
steps.reason: Updating Tally and notifying the customer are repetitive administrative tasks done after LR collection.
steps.idea: Use a Make/Zapier workflow to automatically trigger a WhatsApp template notifying the customer once the LR is attached.

steps.name: Track and Receive Payments
steps.reason: Manual payment follow-ups take continuous effort and often miss aging invoice deadlines.
steps.idea: Set up automated WhatsApp payment reminder alerts using Tally due-date data via a no-code tool.

recommendations.title: AI Purchase Order Capture and Live Stock Checking
recommendations.what_it_does: Automatically extracts order details from incoming customer WhatsApp purchase orders using AI and logs them into a Google Sheet alongside live stock levels fetched directly from Tally. This eliminates the multi-hour manual back-and-forth between staff and the godown to check inventory.
how_it_works: Set up a Make/Zapier workflow connected to your WhatsApp Business API provider (like Interakt or Wati) to catch incoming PO documents or images.
Pass the PO document to an affordable AI document parser (like OpenAI GPT-4o mini) to extract item names and quantities.
Append the extracted order data as a new row in a shared Google Sheet.
Configure a Tally connector (or scheduled script) to sync live inventory levels into the same Google Sheet.
recommendations.human_in_the_loop: Office staff reviews the populated Google Sheet to ensure the AI parsed the PO correctly before proceeding.

replay_rules.why: Live stock levels from Tally are visible immediately in the sheet, removing the 4.8-hour delay for manual stock verification calls.

recommendations.title: Automated Invoice Generation and Smart Auto-Approval
recommendations.what_it_does: Generates draft invoices automatically in Tally based on verified order quantities and applies an auto-approval rule for trusted repeat customers below credit limits. This removes manual data entry and speeds up the approval bottleneck for the business owner.
how_it_works: Create a webhook in Google Sheets that triggers once order quantities and dispatch amounts are finalized.
Use a Tally integration tool to automatically create a draft sales invoice in Tally.
Set up an automation rule checking customer credit limits and past payment history; trusted repeat orders under a specific threshold are auto-approved instantly.
Route only exceptions or high-value orders to the owner via WhatsApp with a 1-click approval button.
recommendations.human_in_the_loop: Business owner manually checks and approves only orders that exceed the set credit limit or come from new customers.

replay_rules.why: Auto-approval rules process trusted repeat customer orders instantly, cutting down the previous 4.3-hour owner review wait.

recommendations.title: Automated Dispatch Notification and Payment Reminders
recommendations.what_it_does: Automatically sends a WhatsApp notification with the LR attachment to the customer once dispatch is updated, and schedules automated payment reminder messages based on Tally due dates. This ensures timely customer communication without manual follow-ups.
how_it_works: Monitor the Google Sheet for the attachment of the LR document by warehouse staff.
Trigger a Make automation to send an approved WhatsApp template message containing the LR details and tracking info to the customer.
Pull invoice due-date data from Tally daily into a tracking sheet.
Automatically trigger polite WhatsApp reminder templates when invoices approach or cross their due dates.
recommendations.human_in_the_loop: Office staff handles direct phone calls if a customer replies with payment disputes or delivery queries.

replay_rules.why: Customer is notified automatically via WhatsApp the moment the LR is attached in the system, removing the manual sending delay.

risks.risk: Customers in this trade frequently negotiate rates or ask for custom discounts on the fly via chat, which static credit rules cannot handle.
risks.mitigation: Route any order where the quoted price differs from the master price list straight to the owner's WhatsApp for manual review.

risks.risk: GST compliance rules require accurate HSN codes and party GSTIN statuses, which automated drafts from messy sheets might get wrong.
risks.mitigation: Lock invoice creation in Tally to only include verified GST-compliant master customer profiles.

risks.risk: Tally connector API failures can create duplicate draft invoices or corrupt ledger entries if webhooks fire twice.
risks.mitigation: Implement a strict unique transaction ID check in the Make scenario before generating the draft in Tally.

critique.who_might_resist: The business owner might resist at first due to a deep-seated fear of an automated rule auto-approving credit for a defaulting client.
critique.change_needed: Set the auto-approval threshold conservatively low so that only 100% trusted, zero-outstanding clients qualify, keeping the owner in control of anything ambiguous.

risks.risk: WhatsApp purchase orders often arrive as blurry photos of handwritten slips or voice notes, which GPT-4o mini will misread.
risks.mitigation: Strictly enforce a rule that POs must be typed text, or route unreadable images directly to staff for manual entry.

risks.risk: Tally running on a local desktop in the office lacks a reliable static IP or constant internet, causing the live stock sync to fail frequently.
risks.mitigation: Use a lightweight local polling script that syncs inventory changes to Google Sheets every 30 minutes rather than relying on real-time webhooks.

risks.risk: During peak festival season, high message volumes will break API rate limits or incur heavy per-message costs.
risks.mitigation: Monitor API usage closely and cap automated parsing to pre-approved regular buyers during peak weeks.

critique.who_might_resist: The godown keeper might resist because they fear losing their gatekeeper status and control over inventory information.
critique.change_needed: Add a mandatory step where office staff must quickly tap a 'Confirm Stock' button before the order is pushed to the sheet, protecting against offline Tally sync errors.

risks.risk: Automated payment reminders sent aggressively via WhatsApp can offend long-standing wholesale clients who expect a human touch during cash crunches.
risks.mitigation: Keep reminder templates polite, and exclude specific VIP accounts from automated messaging based on a tag in Tally.

risks.risk: Warehouse staff will forget or delay attaching the physical LR document in the Google Sheet, breaking the trigger entirely.
risks.mitigation: Make the LR attachment a mandatory field in the staff's daily checklist before they log off.

risks.risk: Hinglish payment disputes replied to by customers will trigger the generic bot loop, frustrating the client further.
risks.mitigation: Ensure incoming replies to payment reminders instantly pause the automation and route the chat to the human office staff.

critique.who_might_resist: Office staff might resist because they worry automated reminders will trigger a flood of irate incoming calls they now have to handle.
critique.change_needed: Add a 'Do Not Remind' toggle tag in Tally for sensitive or negotiating accounts to prevent automated embarrassment.
